description: Only one of the four banks in this cell — Komerční banka — runs a full equity-style IR operation. KB has its own PSE-listed shares and therefore a financial calendar, results presentations, conference calls, a ratings page, a key-figures/fact-book page and a general-meeting record. Česká spořitelna, ČSOB and UniCredit Bank CZ&SK have no listed local equity; their local IR surfaces are thinner and centre on statutory reports plus press releases.

result.result_summary: Extensive cs and en searching found no local quarterly results presentation deck, no earnings call and no analyst-facing fact book for ČS, ČSOB or UniCredit Bank CZ&SK. The presentation layer for ČS sits at Erste Group and for ČSOB at KBC Group; UniCredit Bank CZ&SK has no equivalent at all beyond UniCredit SpA group reporting.

why_it_matters: The cell rationale assumed four comparable structured IR estates with results presentations, fact books and earnings calendars. That holds only for KB. Any collection design that templates 'four banks, same artefact set' will produce three quarters of empty slots. The correct model is: KB local-complete; ČS and ČSOB local-statutory plus parent-group analytical; UniCredit CZ&SK local-statutory only.

description: Every csob.cz URL attempted this session returned HTTP 500 to WebFetch, across three different paths: /portal/csob/vztahy-k-investorum, /csob/povinne-uverejnovane-informace and /csob/servis-pro-media/tiskove-zpravy.

result.result_summary: Three of three fetches failed with HTTP 500. The same pages are indexed by search engines with current content, and ČSOB PDFs on /documents/10710/ are reachable in search results, so the site is live and serving. Recorded as a fetch-method problem, not a dead source.

why_it_matters: ČSOB Group is one of the three largest Czech banking groups; losing it would gut the cell. The blocker is almost certainly header or user-agent filtering on a Liferay portal rather than a real outage, so a headless browser with realistic headers should recover it. Must not be marked dead on this evidence.

description: All unicreditbank.cz HTML pages attempted returned HTTP 403 Forbidden to WebFetch, both the English and Czech annual-reports pages and the debt investor relations page.

result.result_summary: Two of two fetches returned 403. PDFs on the same domain under /content/dam/cee2020-pws-cz/ are indexed and were surfaced with current content by search, which indicates page-level bot defence rather than an unreachable host.

why_it_matters: The document layer is templatable (VZ-YYYY-CZ.pdf, Pololetni-zprava-YYYY-CZE.pdf), so the reports remain collectable via direct asset paths even if the HTML index stays gated. The index page is still needed to discover new filename variants and any prospectus documents.

description: No Czech-language investor-relations landing page could be found for UniCredit Bank Czech Republic and Slovakia. Czech searches on 'vztahy s investory', 'pro investory' and 'tiskové zprávy' scoped to unicreditbank.cz returned only report PDFs and third-party media coverage.

result.result_summary: Czech-language queries surfaced statutory PDFs and an iROZHLAS tag page, but no unicreditbank.cz IR hub or press-release listing. The only investor-facing page located was English-language Debt Investor Relations.

why_it_matters: For this issuer, Czech-language monitoring has to fall back to third-party media and to the Czech editions of the statutory PDFs. There is no local-language IR narrative channel to track, which is itself a finding about how this bank communicates in the CZ market.

description: No RSS, Atom or JSON feed was identified on any of the four banks' IR or press sections.

result.result_summary: Fetches and searches across kb.cz, csas.cz, csob.cz and unicreditbank.cz surfaced no feed endpoint. KB and ČS both expose dated permalink structures that support diff-based change detection instead; ČS additionally has a JSON-backed document SPA whose backing endpoint may serve as a de facto feed if reversed.

why_it_matters: Collection has to be poll-and-diff rather than feed-driven, which raises cost and makes the financial calendars materially more valuable as scheduling inputs. Worth a dedicated check for feed endpoints during the verification pass before committing to polling everywhere.

description: No standalone Pillar 3 / capital adequacy disclosure page was located for any of the four banks, despite targeted Czech searching on 'Pilíř 3' and 'uveřejňování informací'.

result.result_summary: KB's Povinně uveřejňované informace hub lists six children, none of them a Pillar 3 page; the prudential disclosures appear to be folded into 'Informace o bance' or into the annual report. Equivalent pages for the other three were not reachable or not found.

why_it_matters: Pillar 3 tables are the richest comparable prudential dataset across banks (capital ratios, RWA breakdowns, NPL and forbearance, ESG risk templates). If they are embedded in annual-report annexes rather than published standalone, extraction is a PDF-parsing problem rather than a download problem, which changes the collection design and cost.

description: Max banka a.s. is named in this coverage cell as a live second-tier bank, but it is not one. Czech-language searching established that Max banka merged into its parent Banka CREDITAS, ceasing to exist as a separate legal entity with all contractual rights and obligations transferring to Banka CREDITAS; clients kept account numbers while the bank code moved from 4000 to 2250 with a transitional dual-code period. A direct fetch of maxbanka.eu confirmed the site now presents itself as the 'Max' product line of Banka CREDITAS, and its mandatory-disclosure archive stops at the FY2023 annual report and 30 September 2024 quarterly data. Reporting on the exact timing was not fully consistent across the sources found (the legal merger is reported as effective 1 October 2024, while Banka CREDITAS separately describes completing the Max banka integration during 2025), so the precise date should be confirmed against the Sbírka listin merger deed rather than press coverage.

result.result_summary: No live independent Max banka disclosure stream exists. maxbanka.eu remains reachable as a frozen historical archive (annual reports 2010–2023, ČBA-format quarterly filings 2021–Q3 2024) and should be harvested once, now, before decommissioning. Ongoing Max-related disclosure belongs to Banka CREDITAS.

why_it_matters: Scheduling Max banka as a recurring source would produce a permanently stale, silently empty feed and would double-count or misattribute volumes that now sit inside Banka CREDITAS. It also means one of the ten named actors in this cell must be reallocated, and that CREDITAS's balance-sheet and client growth must be read as partly inorganic.

description: Hello bank! (operated in the Czech Republic by BNP Paribas Personal Finance SA, odštěpný závod, bank code 3050, Karla Engliše 3208/5, Prague 5) has exited the Czech market. Czech-language searching found that BNP Paribas Personal Finance announced a controlled wind-down of its Czech operations, stopped opening new accounts and offering further products from early April, sent contract terminations to clients, and provided payment accounts and consumer loans only until the end of November of that wind-down year; the stated rationale was that roughly 300,000 clients was below the scale needed to justify further investment against strong competition. A Komerční banka press release was also found recording an agreement to recommend a new contractual relationship to Hello bank's deposit clients. Searching specifically for a 2026 Hello bank Czech press centre returned no such thing.

result.result_summary: No live Hello bank Czech disclosure or press source exists to track. No Czech statutory annual report exists either, since the entity was an EU single-licence branch (odštěpný závod) rather than a Czech-licensed bank; it is absent from the ČNB list of bank mandatory-disclosure links.

why_it_matters: Hello bank should be dropped from the live monitoring roster and retained only as a historical case study of challenger-bank exit economics in the Czech market. Its client migration is also a concrete competitive event for the surviving banks in this cell, and the Komerční banka arrangement means the beneficiary sits outside this cell in the top-four cell.

description: Both mBank (mBank S.A., organizační složka, IČO 27943445, Pernerova 691/42, Prague 8 – Karlín, operating in the Czech Republic since 2007) and the former Hello bank operate(d) as branches of EU-licensed banks under the single-licence / mutual-recognition regime, supervised primarily by their home regulator. Fetching the ČNB list of bank mandatory-disclosure links confirmed that neither mBank nor BNP Paribas / Hello bank appears among the roughly two dozen banks listed there.

result.result_summary: There is no Czech-law annual report, no local Pillar 3 filing and no local quarterly disclosure annex for mBank CZ. Its financials are only obtainable inside mBank S.A. Group reporting, where the Czech and Slovak branches are disclosed as a combined line within the Retail Banking segment — meaning Czech-only figures generally must be inferred rather than read off.

why_it_matters: Any cross-bank comparison table built from Czech statutory disclosures will silently omit mBank, understating challenger-segment share and distorting market-structure conclusions. Collection for mBank must be designed differently from the other eight actors — parent-group segment extraction plus the Czech press portal — and the CZ/SK aggregation must be flagged as a known precision limit rather than resolved.

description: The ČNB list designates https://www.airbank.cz/dokumenty-ke-stazeni as Air Bank's mandatory-disclosure location. Fetching that page returned only forms, contract documents, the price list, the interest-rate overview, business terms, complaint rules and privacy material. No links to annual reports (výroční zprávy), quarterly disclosure annexes or capital-adequacy data were visible on it, even though Air Bank's consolidated annual report PDFs demonstrably exist on the same host under a /file-download/ path.

result.result_summary: Air Bank's statutory annual reports are retrievable directly by path convention (/file-download/vyrocni-zprava-<YEAR>.pdf, with a numeric-prefixed variant observed for the newest edition) but are not discoverable by crawling the regulator-designated disclosure page. Quarterly and capital-adequacy annexes for Air Bank were not located in this pass at all.

why_it_matters: A collector that trusts the ČNB pointer and crawls only the designated page will conclude Air Bank publishes no annual report — a false negative on one of the cell's most strategically interesting challengers. It also means the regulator's pointer list resolves to a page rather than to a document index, and per-bank crawl rules must be written individually rather than generically.

description: Two priority sources resisted direct fetching in this pass. https://www.creditas.cz/povinne-uverejnovane-informace returned HTTP 403 Forbidden with no body, while individual PDFs on the same host surfaced normally through search — the signature of bot protection rather than absence. https://www.cnb.cz/cs/dohled-financni-trh/informace-zverejnovane-emitenty/ (the Central Repository of Regulated Information) ended in a socket hang up, while several sibling cnb.cz pages fetched successfully in the same session.

result.result_summary: Neither source is recorded as dead. Both are logged as blocked/unverified hypotheses with the observed blocker, and both were routed around: CREDITAS filings are reachable via /files/ document paths and via the Patria regulated-information feed, and the ČNB repository has documented sibling guidance pages that fetched successfully.

why_it_matters: Recording either as dead on a single bad fetch would drop the cell's most active consolidator and the statutory single point of access for regulated information. It also sets the collection requirement: this cell needs a browser-grade fetcher with realistic headers, not a plain HTTP client, and needs redundant paths designed in from the start.

description: Across the eight domestically licensed banks in this cell, only MONETA Money Bank publishes a genuine quarterly earnings package (presentation, interim report, basic-data spreadsheet, press release, conference-call transcript, webcast video) with an investor calendar and sell-side coverage. Raiffeisenbank CZ produces a country-level investor presentation and half-year financial reports; Fio, Trinity Bank, Partners Banka and formerly Max banka publish only the ČNB/ČBA-format quarterly disclosure annexes, which are regulatory data tables with no narrative, no guidance and no management commentary. Air Bank publishes no local quarterly disclosure that was locatable in this pass.

result.result_summary: Topic coverage for 'earnings' and 'investor relations' in this cell is structurally asymmetric: one issuer-grade stream, one partial, and the rest data-only. Narrative and forward-looking signal for the non-listed banks has to be reconstructed from press rooms, parent-group reporting and trade press.

why_it_matters: Analytical expectations must be set accordingly — quarter-by-quarter competitive narrative is available only for MONETA and partly Raiffeisenbank, and any attempt to build a uniform quarterly comparison across the cell will either fail or silently over-weight the one bank that talks. It also means the annual report and press room carry disproportionate weight for six of the nine surviving actors.

description: Several actor names in this cell are seriously noisy in search and need disambiguation before automated collection. 'Partners' collides hard with Partners Group AG (the Swiss private-markets firm) and its SEC filings, and with 'Partners Group Private Equity' funds — an English-language query for Partners investor materials returned mostly Swiss results. 'Raiffeisen' returns Raiffeisen Bank entities in Serbia, Bosnia and elsewhere plus the Austrian parent, and within the Czech Republic alone spans Raiffeisenbank a.s., Raiffeisen investiční společnost, Raiffeisen stavební spořitelna and Raiffeisen – Leasing, each publishing its own výroční zpráva. 'Fio' spans Fio banka, Fio investiční společnost and the Fio brokerage news desk. 'mBank' spans the Polish parent, the Czech branch and the mbank.pl-hosted Czech media portal. 'Trinity' and 'Max' are common words that produce heavy false-positive volume without a bank qualifier.

result.result_summary: Bare-name queries are unusable for automated monitoring in this cell. Reliable retrieval required pairing each name with Czech disclosure vocabulary ('výroční zpráva', 'povinně uveřejňované informace', 'tisková zpráva') and, for the Raiffeisen and Partners families, with the exact legal form ('a.s.', 'Raiffeisenbank a.s.', 'Partners Banka a.s.').

why_it_matters: Without name disambiguation rules and an IČO-anchored actor map, a monitoring pipeline for this cell will ingest Swiss private-equity filings as Czech banking intelligence and will conflate a bank with its sister investment company or building society. This is a design requirement for the collection layer, not a cosmetic issue.

description: The session's WebSearch quota (200/200 calls) was already exhausted by other agents before this cell's first query, so no native web search was available at any point during this run.

result.result_summary: Substituted Seznam.cz HTML search (https://search.seznam.cz/?q=...) fetched via WebFetch as the search engine, supplemented by direct HTTP probing and the ARES REST API. DuckDuckGo (both html. and lite. endpoints) served a CAPTCHA challenge instead of results and was not used; the CAPTCHA was not attempted. Mojeek returned HTTP 403. Seznam.cz worked reliably and is, helpfully, the Czech-market search engine, so local-language recall was good — but result depth was limited to roughly the first page per query, and no result-page pagination was possible.

why_it_matters: Breadth of discovery for this cell is narrower than it should be. Long-tail actors (smaller PSPs, ISOs, bank-internal processing units) and second/third-page results were systematically not seen. A re-run with search budget available should be assumed to add materially to this slice rather than merely confirm it.

description: The seed query used the Czech phrase 'akvizice karetních transakcí' for card acquiring. In Czech financial usage 'akvizice' means a corporate acquisition (M&A), not card acquiring.

result.result_summary: That query returned mostly M&A and unrelated legal/broker results, plus a Euronet merchant-acquiring M&A item. The productive Czech terms are the English loanword 'acquiring' used as-is, and native phrasings 'akceptace platebních karet', 'přijímání platebních karet', 'přijímat platby kartou' and 'zpracování karetních transakcí'. Queries rebuilt on those terms returned the relevant acquirers immediately.

why_it_matters: Any automated collection built on the seed phrasing will have poor precision and will miss the core actors. The glossary for this cell must treat 'akvizice' as a noisy term and prefer 'akceptace/přijímání platebních karet' plus the bare loanword 'acquiring'.

description: Searched in Czech for a Nexi or Nets Czech-language newsroom, press page or local site.

result.result_summary: The Czech query 'Nexi Nets Česká republika platební karty zpracování transakcí' returned only homonyms — a Google Play listing for Nexi Business, an unrelated Czech IT firm 'Nexineo CZ', 'Nexnet', and a real-estate agency 'Reality NEXI'. No Czech-language Nexi/Nets corporate presence was found. The company's existence in Czechia was established only via ARES (Nexi Czech Republic, s.r.o., IČO 27391761, V celnici 1031/4, Praha 1, incorporated 2005-10-31) and its Sbírka listin entry.

why_it_matters: For Nexi there is effectively no Czech-language disclosure channel: coverage must rest on the statutory filings plus the English group newsroom. Also, 'Nexi' and 'Nets' are both high-noise search tokens in Czech and must always be qualified (with 'platební', 's.r.o.', or the IČO) in any automated query.

description: Looked for a Czech-language press/newsroom page belonging to the legal entities Global Payments Europe, s.r.o. and Worldline Czech Republic s.r.o. themselves.

result.result_summary: None found. Global Payments' Czech communication runs through the marketing site globalpayments.cz (which serves HTTP 403 to scripted requests) and its blog; there is no 'tiskové centrum' or press-release archive for the Czech entity. Worldline's Czech site (worldline.com/cs-cz/home) is a localised marketing page, with press releases only at group level in English. The historical domain globalpaymentseurope.cz no longer serves the company — a fetch returned a TLS certificate mismatch, the certificate covering the unrelated names 0oo1.cz / www.0oo1.cz.

why_it_matters: Czech-entity announcements for the two largest actors in this cell are not separately published. Contract wins and platform migrations affecting Czechia must be caught either at parent-group level in English, in the statutory accounts a year later, or indirectly via the SBK/ČTK wires and trade press. Collection design must not assume a local newsroom exists.

description: Several relevant Czech commercial and aggregator domains refused scripted requests.

result.result_summary: HTTP 403 observed on www.globalpayments.cz (root, /blog, /podpora/dulezite-dokumenty), www.gpwebpay.cz, www.zivefirmy.cz and the bare host aktuality.bankovnikarty.cz (though the archive path /akt.htm on that host fetched fine). These are hypotheses of bot defence, not evidence of dead sites — all four appear in current search indexes and one served content on a deeper path.

why_it_matters: Collection for the Global Payments Czech properties requires a headless browser with a realistic fingerprint; a naive HTTP fetcher will silently report these primary sources as unavailable and the cell will look emptier than it is.

description: Multiple plausible URL patterns for corporate and bank press pages returned errors, indicating site re-architecture rather than absence.

result.result_summary: worldline.com/en/home/newsroom.html -> 404 (correct path is /en/home/top-navigation/media-relations); worldline.com/en/home/investors.html -> 400 (IR lives on investors.worldline.com); nexigroup.com/en/media/ and /en/media-and-news/ -> 404 (correct prefix /en/media-relations/); investors.globalpayments.com/financial-information/sec-filings -> 404 (correct path /all-sec-filings); csob.cz/portal/o-csob/pro-media and csob.cz/pro-media -> HTTP 500 redirect to an error page; kb.cz/cs/o-bance/tiskove-centrum, rb.cz/o-nas/pro-media and moneta.cz/o-nas/pro-media -> 404; cnb.cz/cs/statistika/platebni-styk/ -> 404 (statistics sit under /cs/statistika/menova_bankovni_stat/harm_stat_data/); protext.cz/zpravy.php and ceskenoviny.cz/tiskove/ -> 404 while the deeper paths work.

why_it_matters: Per the playbook these are hypotheses, not verdicts. Every one of them was resolved to a live path by re-deriving from site navigation or a fresh search — so any monitoring config must include a re-discovery step on 404 instead of retiring the source. The ČSOB HTTP 500 in particular should be retried before any conclusion.

description: Checked whether the CardMag trade-magazine public PDF archive extends to recent years.

result.result_summary: The archive index at cardmag.cz/pages/cze/archiv.html enumerates issues in the pattern cm<quarter>_<year>.pdf and the visible listing runs to 2018. Probes for cm2_2025.pdf and cm1_2026.pdf both returned HTTP 404. Whether the magazine ceased, moved behind a member wall, or simply changed its filename scheme was not determined.

why_it_matters: CardMag is the deepest narrative source on Czech card processing history, so a truncated archive caps its usefulness for recent-period analysis while leaving it excellent for reconstructing the MUZO/Global Payments Europe lineage and older bank-processor relationships. Worth one targeted follow-up to establish the current publication status.

description: The SBK association site links a members-only data area.

result.result_summary: http://data.bankovnikarty.cz/secure/private.htm is linked from the SBK home page as a restricted area. It was not accessed and no credentials were sought.

why_it_matters: The richest granular Czech card statistics (likely including per-member acquiring data) are behind association membership. Open collection is limited to the published aggregate statistics and quarterly press releases; anything finer would require a legitimate membership or a commercial data agreement, which is a procurement decision rather than a collection one.

description: Two Czech public registers relevant to contract evidence could not be reached from this environment.

result.result_summary: smlouvy.gov.cz (Registr smluv) timed out twice with zero bytes received (curl exit 28) despite a deep contract permalink appearing as a live indexed search result; vestnikverejnychzakazek.cz failed to connect (HTTP 000). Both are recorded as unverified, not dead.

why_it_matters: The contracts register is one of the highest-value indirect sources for this cell because it exposes actual acquiring contract terms signed by public-sector merchants. Its apparent unavailability is very likely an artefact of this sandbox's network rather than the source, and it must be re-checked from a normal network before any judgement is made about it.

description: The session's WebSearch budget (200/200 calls) was already fully consumed before this cell's first query was issued. BOTH planned cs and en searches ('ComGate platební brána tisková zpráva objem transakcí', 'GoPay platební brána novinky tiskové zprávy e-shop') returned a budget-exhausted notice and performed no search. All 25 candidates in this slice were therefore discovered by direct WebFetch of hypothesised URLs plus link-following and snowballing, not by search-engine discovery.

result.result_summary: Zero successful WebSearch calls. ~30 WebFetch calls executed instead, of which the large majority returned usable content; discovery proceeded by first-principles URL hypothesis + footer/nav link-following + snowballing from press-release contents.

why_it_matters: Snowballing from known actors is strong for depth but systematically weak for DISCOVERY of unknown small actors. Long-tail CZ gateways and small e-money institutions that are not linked from any page I fetched are almost certainly missing. The cell should be re-run with search budget available before its coverage is treated as complete.

description: ThePay, a.s. (IČO 28135261, Jihlava) — one of the four named domestic gateway brands in this cell — publishes no blog, no novinky and no tiskové zprávy. Both the homepage (thepay.eu, reached via 301 from thepay.cz) and the contact page were inspected; the footer offers only nápověda, kontakt, pdf-verze and partnerský program.

result.result_summary: Local-language terms 'novinky' and 'tiskové zprávy' were searched for on the site and are absent. No press contact published.

why_it_matters: ThePay cannot be tracked via corporate communications at all. Intelligence on this actor must come entirely from statutory filings (Sbírka listin, IČO 28135261) and third-party trade press. Any collection plan that assumes a press-release feed per gateway will silently produce a blind spot on ThePay.

description: Stripe's newsroom country/language selector was inspected and lists numerous European markets (Poland, Austria, Germany and others) but NO Czech Republic option; no cs-localised newsroom or Czech-specific press content was found. Likewise Adyen's press-and-media page has no regional filtering for Europe/CEE/Czech Republic and is a contact/press-kit hub rather than a dated release archive.

result.result_summary: Two of the three named international players (Stripe, Adyen) have NO Czech local press room. The third (Revolut) could not be checked because the newsroom returned HTTP 403.

why_it_matters: The cell brief assumes 'local press rooms of Adyen, Stripe and Revolut Business' exist. For Adyen and Stripe they do not. Their CZ activity must instead be inferred from product/docs surfaces (supported countries, local payment methods, CZK settlement, local acquiring) and from CZ trade press — a materially different and more fragile collection method than press-release monitoring.

description: Two sources expected to carry payment-mix data did not. (1) Comgate's blog contains product announcements and merchant case studies but NO posts on transaction volumes, instant payments, payment-method mix or e-commerce statistics; the only volume reference found was qualitative, in 'Rok 2025 v Comgate' (2026-01-23), which mentions growth in payment volume and client count without figures. (2) Shoptet's press page carries merchant-base growth and Black Friday data but NO payment-method-mix or online-payment-adoption statistics.

result.result_summary: The 'gateways publish payment mix' hypothesis is only weakly supported. Hard numbers found across the whole cell were sparse and mostly on About/media pages rather than in releases: Comgate 23k e-shops / 10k terminals / CZK 616.6m registered capital / 80 staff / 20 years; GoPay 18k e-shops CZ+SK, 11k merchants Central Europe, CZK 90bn volume target for 2025; Twisto 17k e-shops and 600k users (2019); Besteron 6,100+ clients.

why_it_matters: Instant-payment adoption and payment-method mix — two of the highest-value signals this cell was scoped to reveal — are NOT reliably published by the gateways themselves. Those metrics will have to come from ČNB payment statistics, APEK research, or bank-side reporting, meaning this cell should be treated as an actor/merchant-win/product-roadmap sensor rather than as a payment-mix data source.

description: The ČNB open-data page was inspected specifically for downloadable CSV lists of platební instituce and instituce elektronických peněz. The datasets actually enumerated were banks and foreign bank branches, směnárny, non-bank consumer-credit providers and consumer-credit intermediaries. No payment-institution or e-money-institution CSV was listed. Licence terms for reuse were also not stated anywhere on the page.

result.result_summary: Payment-institution open data not confirmed to exist. The JERRS.OPENDATA.STAHUJ?p_seznam=N endpoint pattern was observed, so other list ids may exist, but this is an untested hypothesis.

why_it_matters: The cheap open-data path to the CZ payment-institution actor map is not confirmed. The fallback, WS JERRS, requires a commercial certificate and a signed registration request to jerrsws@cnb.cz — a procurement lead time that should be started early rather than discovered late.

description: https://www.revolut.com/news/ returned HTTP 403 Forbidden with no body. Per method this is recorded as a bot-defence hypothesis, NOT as a dead source. Whether Revolut operates a cs-CZ localised newsroom, and whether Revolut Business CZ announcements appear there, could not be determined.

result.result_summary: One of the three named international press rooms is unreadable by plain HTTP fetch and requires a browser-based collector.

why_it_matters: Revolut is a significant CZ market participant and Revolut Business is directly in scope for merchant acceptance. Leaving this unresolved is a real coverage hole, and the fix (headless browser) is a different collector class from the rest of this slice.

description: Several hypothesised URLs returned 404 or redirected, and are recorded here so they are not mistaken for dead sources: comgate.cz/blog 301 -> comgate.eu/cs/blog which then 404s (the real blog is /cs/blog-o-platebnich-sluzbach); comgate.eu/cs/zminili-se-o-nas 404s although the pro-media page references a 'Zmínili se o nás' media-mentions page (correct slug unknown); cnb.cz/cs/dohled-financni-trh/seznamy/jerrs/ (trailing slash) 404s; corporate.payu.com/newsroom/ 404s (correct path is /media-and-press/); thepay.cz 301 -> thepay.eu; besteron.cz 301 -> besteron.com/cz/; apl.cnb.cz 301 -> jerrs.cnb.cz.

result.result_summary: Domain migrations are widespread in this cell — three of the five domestic actors have moved from .cz to .eu/.com domains, and ČNB has moved its register application host.

why_it_matters: Any historical link list for CZ gateways is likely stale. Collectors must follow redirects and must not treat a 404 on a guessed slug as evidence a section does not exist. The unresolved 'Zmínili se o nás' page in particular is a lost third-party-coverage index for Comgate.

description: IČO/registration identifiers could not be established from the companies' own sites for several in-cell actors: PayU's Czech legal entity name and IČO are absent from czech.payu.com; Besteron's site gives the NBS permit number (ODB-6111/2015-7) and the name 'Besteron A.S.' but no IČO/IČO SK; GoPay's site does not display an IČO for the odštěpný závod. Confirmed identifiers found: Comgate a.s. IČ 279 24 505 / DIČ CZ27924505; ThePay, a.s. IČO 28135261 / DIČ CZ28135261; Skip Pay s.r.o. IČO 07093331; Global payments Europe, s.r.o. (address only).

result.result_summary: Only 4 of ~8 CZ-relevant entities have a confirmed registration identifier from primary sources.

why_it_matters: The IČO is the join key between the marketing layer (press rooms) and the statutory layer (Sbírka listin, JERRS). Without it, annual reports and licence records cannot be automatically linked to the right brand, and brand-to-entity mapping errors are likely (e.g. GoPay's CZ branch vs its foreign parent).

description: The session's WebSearch budget was already fully consumed (200 of 200 calls) before this cell began, so not a single search-engine query could be executed. The mandated cs/en dual-language query sweep — including the supplied seed queries and the extensions prepared for them — was therefore never run.

result.result_summary: Zero search-engine queries executed. All discovery was carried out by direct HTTP fetching of hypothesised URLs plus link-following (snowball) from fetched pages, with first-principles reasoning about who must publish, who benefits, who regulates and who aggregates used to generate the initial URL hypotheses. Czech-language coverage was still achieved, but through Czech-language site navigation and Czech terminology in URL construction rather than through Czech-language search queries.

why_it_matters: Snowball-from-known-actors is systematically biased toward incumbents with good websites. It will under-discover small, new or low-web-presence providers, regional media, court and enforcement records, and any actor not linked from a page already visited. The cell's actor map should be regarded as strong on the majors and thin on the tail until a search sweep is run.

description: Cofidis CZ (COFIDIS a.s.) clearly maintains a news/press area — the homepage 'O nás' navigation lists novinky (news) alongside corporate responsibility and awards — but the actual URL could not be resolved.

result.result_summary: Four candidate paths were fetched and all returned HTTP 404: https://www.cofidis.cz/tiskove-zpravy, https://www.cofidis.cz/o-nas, https://www.cofidis.cz/o-nas.html and https://www.cofidis.cz/cs/o-nas/novinky.html. A sitemap fetch at https://www.cofidis.cz/sitemap.xml also returned HTTP 404.

description: Raiffeisenbank CZ's media centre could not be located, which matters because its PlatímPak BNPL brand publishes no press releases of its own — platimpak.cz/pro-media offers only a spokesperson contact, two logo versions and a brand manual PDF, and explicitly points readers to the bank's own media centre.

result.result_summary: Both https://www.rb.cz/o-nas/pro-media and https://www.rb.cz/o-nas/pro-media/tiskove-zpravy returned HTTP 404. The only confirmed rb.cz path found was the privacy page linked from platimpak.cz: https://www.rb.cz/informacni-servis/ochrana-osobnich-udaju, suggesting the site uses an /informacni-servis/ style hierarchy that was not further explored.

why_it_matters: PlatímPak is a bank-owned deferred-payment arm sitting squarely in this cell, and without the parent bank's press channel there is no release-level feed for it at all.

description: Zonky no longer operates as an independent publisher. Its site footer reads '© 2026 Air Bank a.s., člen skupiny PPF, poskytovatel služby Zonky', and its navigation contains no press, media, news or blog section at all — only o-zonky, kontakty, poradna, dokumenty, cenik and an affiliate programme.
