description: None of the Czech-domiciled specialists in this cell publish annual reports or audited financial statements on their own websites. Home Credit a.s.'s /o-nas page carries a legal-entity identity (IČO 269 78 636, Brno, PPF group, ČNB-authorised as payment institution and non-bank consumer-credit provider) and a client ombudsman, but no reports; ESSOX, Twisto, Skip Pay and PlatímPak similarly expose only terms, pricing and press material.

result.result_summary: Confirmed across homecredit.cz, essox.cz, twisto.cz, skippay.cz and platimpak.cz: no výroční zpráva or účetní závěrka links found on any of them.

why_it_matters: It means the financial-statement layer for this entire cell depends on the Sbírka listin and on foreign parent disclosures (PPF, Home Credit Group, KBC/ČSOB, Inbank Group, Param). Collection design must treat the register as the primary financial source rather than as a fallback.

description: Two important register/statistics endpoints returned essentially no content to a plain HTTP fetch: https://dataor.justice.cz/ returned only the header 'Opendata', and https://www.cnb.cz/arad/ returned only 'ČNB ARAD'. The new unified register portal https://verejnerejstriky.msp.gov.cz/ rendered only partially.

result.result_summary: Content is almost certainly assembled client-side. This is a rendering hypothesis, not evidence that the services are unavailable — the ČNB and Ministry of Justice endpoints are official infrastructure and should be assumed live.

why_it_matters: These are exactly the machine-readable, licence-clean sources the collection layer should prefer over scraping corporate sites. Getting them working requires a headless browser or the documented data/API endpoints, and that work should be planned rather than discovered late.

description: No Czech trade association, self-regulatory body or code of conduct specific to BNPL or deferred payment was located. The nearest structures found were ČLFA (broad non-bank finance and consumer credit, which does include Twisto Payments a.s. as a member) and SOLUS (credit registries).

result.result_summary: Searched by navigation and by reasoning about who would organise such a body; found none. Czech BNPL providers appear to organise through the general non-bank finance association rather than a BNPL-specific one.

why_it_matters: There is no single BNPL-sector voice publishing volume or conduct data for Czechia, so sector aggregation must be assembled from ČLFA statistics, ČNB supervisory material and APEK e-commerce studies rather than from a dedicated body.

description: Two attempts to reach general search infrastructure and one foreign issuer site were repelled by bot defences.

result.result_summary: https://html.duckduckgo.com/html/ returned a CAPTCHA challenge page ('Please complete the following challenge...', error code 90d2) instead of results, closing off the workaround for the exhausted WebSearch budget. https://www.ipfin.co.uk/en/investors.html returned a page containing only 'Challenge Validation'.

why_it_matters: Confirms that search-engine-based discovery was genuinely unavailable on this pass, and flags IPF as needing a browser-grade fetcher or an RNS-feed route in the collection layer.

description: The session's WebSearch budget (200/200 calls) was already exhausted before this cell's first query was issued, so none of the assigned cs/en seed queries could actually be run. All discovery was performed instead by direct HTTP fetching of known operator domains, HTML link extraction, meta-refresh/redirect following and snowballing (ČNB nav -> CERTIS subpages; SBK homepage -> 531-PDF press archive, CardMag, ČBA; ARES API -> Sbírka listin). Consequently the queries_used fields are legitimately empty rather than fabricated.

result.result_summary: 0 web searches executed; ~40 direct fetches/status probes executed instead. Coverage of the cell's core actors was achieved, but long-tail recall that keyword search would have surfaced is likely missing.

why_it_matters: Recall risk: sources that are not reachable by guessing a domain or by following a link from an already-known Czech payments site are systematically under-represented in this slice. Re-run the cell with search enabled to close the tail.

description: Mastercard's Czech localised estate refuses automated fetches. https://www.mastercard.cz/cs-cz/o-nas/tiskove-centrum.html and https://www.mastercard.cz/cs-cz/podnikatele/podpora/mezibankovni-poplatky.html both returned HTTP 403 with no body, to WebFetch and to curl with a desktop Chrome user-agent. https://www.mastercard.com/news/europe/cs-cz/ also returned 403.

result.result_summary: 403 on every Mastercard CZ path attempted. Not treated as dead: 403-with-no-body is the classic edge/bot-defence signature, and the domain is still linked as current from Czech trade sites (bankovnikarty.cz, cardmag.cz).

why_it_matters: Mastercard is half of the duopoly this cell exists to track. Until a headless-browser collector is in place, Mastercard CZ coverage depends on the SBK/CardMag TZ_MasterCard_*.pdf mirror archive, which is a third-party mirror with unknown completeness.

description: Czech-looking localised paths on visa.cz do not exist: /o-visa/tiskove-centrum.html and /o-visa/novinky.html both return 404. The working Czech newsroom sits on an English path, https://www.visa.cz/about-visa/newsroom.html, while individual releases live under /o-spolecnosti-visa/newsroom/press-releases.NNNNNNN.html — a third path prefix.

result.result_summary: Two guessed Czech paths 404; the real newsroom (200, Czech-language content) was found by probing the English path. Three inconsistent path prefixes coexist on the same host.

why_it_matters: Any collector built on 'localise the path' heuristics will silently miss Visa CZ entirely and may record it as a dead source. Pin the discovered URLs and re-derive detail-page links from the listing rather than constructing them.

description: The acronym APMS (apms.cz), linked from the SBK homepage among payments-industry links, is NOT a payments body. It is the Asociace provozovatelů mobilních sítí — the Czech mobile network operators' association (O2, T-Mobile, Vodafone; IČO 75118891), concerned with telecom infrastructure.

result.result_summary: Fetched and confirmed off-topic. Excluded from candidates.

why_it_matters: Noisy term for this cell: Czech payments sources cross-link telecom bodies (mobile payments context), and an unchecked acronym expansion would pollute the actor map. Flag APMS as excluded in the cell glossary.

description: No Czech-entity annual report, statutory financial statement or CZ-level investor-relations disclosure was found for Visa or Mastercard's Czech operations. Both schemes publish only marketing press releases locally; financial disclosure sits at group level. investor.visa.com and investor.mastercard.com both returned HTTP 403 to automated fetches (bot defence assumed, not verified as dead).

result.result_summary: Zero CZ-specific scheme financial disclosures located; group IR portals unreachable by automated fetch.

why_it_matters: The 'annual reports / investor relations / earnings' topics in this run's scope cannot be satisfied from CZ scheme entities. For scheme economics, the run must fall back to group SEC filings (10-K/10-Q) or to interchange-fee regulatory disclosures, neither of which was located for CZ in this pass.

description: ČNB's oversight page states that PFMI-based assessments of CERTIS (2023, previously 2016) and of the SKD securities settlement system (2023, previously 2018) were completed, but publishes no link to the assessment documents themselves.

result.result_summary: Assessment existence confirmed in prose; assessment documents not located on the oversight page.

why_it_matters: The most substantive independent evaluation of the national clearing rail is referenced but not retrievable from the obvious location. Worth a targeted follow-up (ČNB annual report chapters, or an information request) rather than assuming the documents are unpublished.

description: Bankovní identita, a.s. publishes no výroční zpráva (annual report) or financial statements on bankid.cz. The /pro-akcionare/ page held exactly one artefact, a general-meeting ZIP for September 2026, and no shareholder-bank list.

result.result_summary: Self-published financial disclosure absent; statutory route via Sbírka listin (IČO 09513817, confirmed via ARES) is the only identified path.

why_it_matters: Bank iD's economics and ownership structure — which banks hold what share of the national identity rail — are only obtainable with the 6-12 month lag of statutory filings, not from the operator's own site. Plan collection accordingly.

description: https://www.praguepaymentsweek.com/ (Czech payments industry conference, linked from both bankovnikarty.cz and cardmag.cz) timed out after 25 seconds with no response.

result.result_summary: Connection timeout, HTTP code 000. Recorded as unverified, not dead — a single timeout is not evidence of removal, and the site may simply be dormant between editions.

why_it_matters: Conference programmes are a good pointer source for which scheme and infrastructure topics the Czech industry is prioritising, and for speaker-level actor mapping. Worth a retry from a different network before writing it off.

description: The ČNB ARAD statistical database (https://www.cnb.cz/arad/) is a JavaScript single-page application. A plain fetch returned only the shell 'ČNB ARAD' with no dataset content, so the structure of set D458 (CERTIS statistics, referenced by name from the CERTIS statistics page) could not be inspected, nor could the export formats or any API endpoint be confirmed.

result.result_summary: Dataset identifier D458 confirmed from the ČNB CERTIS page; dataset contents and export mechanics unconfirmed.

why_it_matters: The machine-readable route to Czech clearing volumes is identified but not yet specified. A headless-browser or network-trace pass is needed to capture ARAD's underlying JSON endpoint before this can become an automated feed.

description: Guessed paths that do not exist and should not be re-probed: https://www.cnb.cz/cs/platebni-styk/okamzite-platby/ (404 — the real path is nested under /certis/), https://www.cnb.cz/cs/dohled-financni-trh/vykon-dohledu/dohled-nad-platebnimi-systemy/ (404 — oversight lives at /cs/platebni-styk/oversight/, an English word inside a Czech path), https://cbaonline.cz/tiskove-zpravy (soft 404 page), https://newsroom.mastercard.com/eu/ and /news/eu/en/ (404 — no country-level Mastercard newsroom found).

result.result_summary: Five plausible-looking paths confirmed non-existent; correct paths recorded in the candidate entries.

why_it_matters: Documents the dead ends so a later run does not spend budget rediscovering them, and shows that ČNB mixes English slugs ('oversight') into Czech URL trees — path-localisation heuristics are unreliable on cnb.cz too.

description: Both bankovnikarty.cz and cardmag.cz emit malformed links to recent Mastercard press releases, missing the slash after the hostname: 'http://aktuality.bankovnikarty.czTZ_MasterCard_18-08-2026.pdf' and '...czTZ_MasterCard_20-08-2026.pdf'. The equivalent Visa link on the same pages is well-formed and fetches successfully (297 KB PDF).

result.result_summary: Two current Mastercard TZ links are unfetchable as published; the repaired form is the obvious fix but was not exercised.

why_it_matters: A naive crawler will silently drop the newest Mastercard items from the very archive being used to work around the mastercard.cz 403 — compounding the Mastercard coverage gap. The collector must normalise these hrefs.

description: The SBK and CardMag estates are legacy static sites: the apex URLs serve only a meta-refresh redirect to /pages/czech/home.html and /pages/cze/home.html respectively, content is encoded in windows-1250 rather than UTF-8, the news archive is served over plain HTTP only, and pages carry FrontPage-era markup. WebFetch returned empty content for both apex URLs; only raw curl plus explicit iconv decoding worked.

result.result_summary: Both sites confirmed live (HTTP 200) and content-rich once the redirect and encoding are handled, but invisible to a standard fetch-and-parse pipeline.

why_it_matters: The single best CZ card-statistics series and the largest Czech scheme press archive would both be scored as empty or dead by a default collector. Encoding and meta-refresh handling must be explicit for this cell.

description: For the SEPA scheme layer (European Payments Council) and the comparative payments statistics layer (ECB Data Portal), no Czech-language version was found — both publish in English only. No Czech-language SEPA scheme rulebook or Czech national SEPA coordination portal was located in this pass.

result.result_summary: SEPA/EU-level sources are en-only in this slice; the cs-language SEPA layer is unfilled.

why_it_matters: The run mandates cs coverage. If a Czech SEPA coordination body or Czech-language rulebook translation exists (plausibly hosted by ČBA), it was not found here and remains an open gap rather than a confirmed absence.

description: The WebSearch tool reported its per-session budget fully consumed (200/200) before this cell's first query, so all discovery had to be routed through WebFetch against public search engines. DuckDuckGo (html and lite endpoints) returned an anti-bot CAPTCHA challenge, which I did not attempt to solve, and Mojeek returned HTTP 403. Seznam.cz (search.seznam.cz) fetched successfully and became the sole discovery engine for this slice.

result.result_summary: All 16 discovery queries in this slice were executed through search.seznam.cz via WebFetch; ~10 results per query, first page only. No Google/Bing/DuckDuckGo coverage and no deep result pages.

why_it_matters: Seznam's index is strong for Czech-language consumer and corporate content but weaker for English-language financial disclosure, PDF-embedded content and international trade press. Sources findable only via Google/Bing (e.g. ATMIA and international cash-industry publications, English-language CEE ATM market reporting) are systematically underrepresented in this slice, and no result set went past page one.

description: Targeted Czech-language searching for a non-bank ATM deployer other than Euronet ('nebankovní bankomat', 'nezávislá síť bankomatů Česko', 'konkurence Euronetu', 'provozovatel bankomatů', 'nezávislý provozovatel bankomatů v obcích') surfaced no second independent deployer of any scale. Results returned only Euronet properties, Euronet fee criticism, bank ATM listings and map POIs.

result.result_summary: No Czech IAD competitor to Euronet identified. Euronet's own June 2026 statement — ~10% of all Czech ATMs, ~300 of ~1,200 machines in Prague — is currently the only quantified deployer-share figure found.

why_it_matters: If confirmed, the Czech independent-deployer market is effectively single-operator, which concentrates the entire non-bank ATM intelligence problem on one company and its parent filings, and makes the Sbírka listin filing of Euronet Services (IČO 25608452) disproportionately important. It also means fleet-share claims come from an interested party with no rival source to triangulate against.

description: The status of G4S's Czech cash business could not be resolved. brinks.cz publishes a post about a partnership with 'G4S Secure Solutions (CZ) a.s.' framed as a security-services cooperation, and two Brink's cash entities are registered in Czechia (Brink's Cash Solutions (CZ) a.s., IČO 27590151, incorporated 2006-09-01; Brink's Cash Solutions Services (CZ) s.r.o., IČO 08829969, incorporated 2020-01-08, the latter's incorporation date being consistent with a carve-in around the Brink's–G4S cash transaction period). No document was found confirming whether G4S's Czech cash-in-transit operation was transferred to Brink's, retained, or wound down.

result.result_summary: G4S Cash Solutions as a distinct Czech CIT operator was not located; only G4S Secure Solutions (CZ) a.s. appears, as a Brink's partner in guarding-type services. Relationship unconfirmed.

why_it_matters: Whether the Czech CIT market is a two-player (Loomis/Brink's) or three-player structure changes any read on pricing power and on bank outsourcing leverage. Getting this wrong would misstate the competitive baseline for the entire cash-logistics side of this cell.

description: Sdružení pro bankovní karty (bankovnikarty.cz), historically the canonical publisher of total Czech ATM counts covering the whole estate rather than only bank-operated machines, shows detailed statistics only through roughly 2011–2012 on its Czech market profile page, despite the page carrying a recent 'aktualizováno' stamp.

result.result_summary: Latest detailed series observed: 10.03m cards, 4,082 ATMs, 69,878 merchant locations, 59,836 POS terminals, with trend data spanning 2001–2011.

why_it_matters: This removes the one industry series that historically counted all ATMs regardless of owner. It is the direct cause of the fleet-attribution gap in this cell: ČNB counts bank-operated ATMs only, so without SBK there is no authoritative published split between bank-owned and deployer-owned machines.

description: No published ČNB list of persons authorised to process domestic banknotes and coins (a register of cash-processing companies) was located. The ČNB legislation section yields the Act on the circulation of banknotes and coins, professional-course requirements and the tested-device lists, and portal.gov.cz documents an information-provision duty toward ČNB, but no public roster of processors was found.

result.result_summary: Found instead: two device registries (banknote and coin processing equipment) and a gov.cz service page describing reporting to ČNB. No entity-level register of cash processors surfaced.

why_it_matters: A processor register would be the cleanest possible census of the Czech cash-handling industry, including small and regional operators invisible to media and to financial-sector lists. Its absence forces reliance on CZ-NACE sweeps in ARES and on security-industry association directories, both noisier.

description: Four fetches failed and are recorded as hypotheses, not verdicts: ir.euronetworldwide.com (landing page and /news-events/press-releases) and investors.brinks.com both timed out at 60s; smlouvy.gov.cz search UI timed out at 60s; www.sec.gov EDGAR browse-edgar returned HTTP 403.

result.result_summary: None of these was confirmed dead. The SEC 403 is the expected response to a request without a compliant declared User-Agent under SEC access policy; the timeouts are consistent with CDN/bot defence or slow server-side rendering. smlouvy.gov.cz content was independently observed as indexed and reachable via search results (individual contract URLs appeared).

why_it_matters: These four are among the highest-value disclosure endpoints in the cell. Recording them as dead would wrongly drop parent-level and contract-level intelligence; the correct next step is a fetch with a declared User-Agent and longer timeout, or use of the documented APIs and open-data dumps rather than the web UIs.

description: No Czech-language term, association or portal specific to cash-in-transit or ATM deployment as an industry was found. Searches on 'převoz cenin', 'komora podniků komerční bezpečnosti', 'asociace bezpečnostních služeb' returned only the general commercial-security chamber KPKB ČR and allied bodies, whose published partner list did not include Loomis, Brink's, G4S or Securitas.

result.result_summary: Czech CIT appears to have no dedicated sectoral association or trade portal; it sits inside the broader commercial-security industry vocabulary ('ostraha majetku a osob', 'převoz cenin', 'bezpečnostní služby').

why_it_matters: There is no single local-language hub to snowball from for cash logistics, so actor discovery for smaller CIT firms must come from CZ-NACE sweeps in ARES, procurement award notices and security-association member directories rather than from an industry body.

description: No Czech Banking Association API standard or open-data feed for ATM and branch locations was found. Searching in Czech for 'standard API bankomaty pobočky open data lokality' returned only consumer directories (banky.cz, penize.cz, airbank.cz map pages), with the engine explicitly flagging that results did not contain the API/association/open-data terms.

result.result_summary: No PSD2-style or association-standard ATM-locator open dataset located for Czechia in this run.

why_it_matters: A standard locator feed would give exact, operator-attributed fleet data at near-zero collection cost. Without it, fleet mapping falls back to OpenStreetMap extracts and sampled directory scraping, which are less complete and carry licensing constraints.

description: No bank–ATM operator outsourcing contract or announcement was found in Czech-language searching ('banka outsourcing bankomatů smlouva Euronet MONETA Raiffeisenbank provoz sítě'). Euronet markets 'Outsourcing bankomatů' and 'Dohoda o účasti v síti' on its own /banky/ page, but no counterparty bank was named in any public source located.

result.result_summary: Outsourcing offer confirmed on the deployer side; no named Czech bank counterparty found in public sources.

why_it_matters: Bank-to-deployer outsourcing is the single most consequential structural variable in this cell — it determines how much of the bank fleet is really deployer-run. That it is undisclosed on both sides means it must be inferred indirectly (Sbírka listin narratives, related-party notes, procurement records, field observation of operator branding on machines).

description: The session's WebSearch budget was already fully consumed (200 of 200 calls) before this cell began. Every planned Czech-language and English seed query — 'Asseco Central Europe tiskova zprava banka implementace', 'Trask Solutions pripadova studie banka reference', and the remaining seed and extension queries — was refused by the tool with a budget message, not executed.

result.result_summary: Zero search queries executed. All discovery in this slice was performed by direct URL fetching of seed-actor domains, sitemap enumeration, redirect-chain following and navigation snowballing. The queries_used field is therefore empty on every candidate — this is an honest empty, not an omission.

why_it_matters: The routine mandates local-language search. Fetch-and-snowball recovers the known actors and their structures well, but it cannot surface unknown vendors, one-off press releases carried only by third parties, or bank-project stories on sites nobody thought to guess. Recall in this cell should be assumed materially below what a searched run would achieve, and the cell should be re-run with search budget available.

description: The coverage cell pairs 'Aricoma/Cleverlance' as one actor. A fetch of https://www.cleverlance.com/ returned HTTP 301 to https://www.avenga.com/ — not to Aricoma. Avenga's own site lists Prague, Brno and Ostrava offices and financial clients including Raiffeisen Bank, UniCredit, Generali and Fidelity.

result.result_summary: Cleverlance's web identity now resolves to Avenga, a separate group from Aricoma/KKCG. Aricoma (aricoma.com, KKCG technology division) is a distinct live actor with its own newsroom and customer wall.

why_it_matters: Treating Cleverlance as an Aricoma sub-brand would silently drop a whole delivery organisation with substantial Czech banking history from the monitored set, and would mis-attribute past Cleverlance bank projects to the wrong corporate parent. Both aricoma.com and avenga.com must be tracked separately.

description: Trask appears to have retired its Czech-language web presence. https://www.trask.cz/ issues a 301 to https://www.thetrask.com/, and both https://www.thetrask.com/cs and https://www.thetrask.com/cz returned HTTP 404. All observed navigation and content paths use the /en/ prefix.

result.result_summary: No Czech-language Trask site path was found. Trask content is collected in English only.

why_it_matters: Trask is the single richest source of Czech bank project disclosure in this cell, yet it now publishes in English only. Anyone monitoring by Czech keywords alone will miss it entirely, and Czech-language name variants of banks (e.g. 'Ceska sporitelna' vs 'Ceska Sporitelna'/'CS') will not match. Monitoring rules for Trask must be English-keyword-based, which is the opposite of the default assumption for a Czech vendor.

description: CCA Group (cca.cz) is live and well-structured in Czech, but its published reference set contains no banking or financial-institution clients. Observed references are the Ministry of Justice (information systems since 1995), the Czech Office for Surveying and Cadastre, the Ministry of Finance gambling-oversight system AISG, and SKODA JS ERP.

result.result_summary: CCA Group verified as a live actor but not currently a bank-technology disclosure channel; it reads as a public-sector and industrial custom-software house.

why_it_matters: The cell definition assumes all ten seed vendors are bank-technology suppliers. At least one is not, on its own public evidence. Spending equal crawl budget across all ten would waste effort; CCA should drop to low-frequency keyword-triggered monitoring rather than routine collection.

description: Aricoma's press-release stream carries no banking items in its recent output. The three most recent releases observed on both the EN (/press-releases) and CS (/cs/tiskove-zpravy) indexes are the Dentsu Tracking acquisition (01/08/2026), the acquisition of SAP suppliers in Austria and Slovenia (08/01/2026) and the consolidation of its SAP companies (01/01/2026). Separately, the /case-studies index exposes a 'Banks and Insurance Companies' branch filter but the default listing surfaced no banking case studies among 20+ visible items.

result.result_summary: Aricoma's banking relationships are visible on its customer wall (CSOB Group, Ceska sporitelna, Raiffeisenbank, ING, Citibank) but are not narrated in recent press releases or in the unfiltered case-study listing.

why_it_matters: For Czech bank projects Aricoma discloses relationships, not projects — the customer wall carries the signal while the newsroom carries M&A. Collection should weight the customer wall and the filtered case-study view over the press feed, and the filtered branch view must be fetched explicitly because the default listing hides it.

description: Asseco properties refused plain HTTP fetches. https://ce.asseco.com/ and https://ce.asseco.com/en/news/ both returned HTTP 403 Forbidden with no body; https://asseco.com/investor-relations/ and https://inwestor.asseco.com/en/ likewise returned 403. The legacy domain https://www.asseco-ce.com/cz/ returned a 302 to ce.asseco.com, confirming an intentional, maintained domain migration.

result.result_summary: Asseco Central Europe and Asseco Poland IR are recorded as unverified-blocked, NOT dead. A maintained 302 from the legacy domain is positive evidence the estate is live and actively managed; a blanket 403 across four unrelated paths on two hosts is the signature of a WAF, not of removed content.

why_it_matters: Asseco Central Europe is arguably the most important single actor in this cell — a core-banking supplier across CZ/SK whose parent is WSE-listed and therefore subject to audited segment disclosure. Losing it to a premature 'dead' verdict would gut the cell. Re-attempt with a headless browser; if the issuer site stays blocked, route to the regulated WSE/ESPI filing channel, which is the more durable path regardless.

description: GEM System could not be characterised. Four URL variants — https://www.gemsystem.cz/, https://gemsystem.cz/, https://www.gemsystem.cz/cz/ and https://www.gemsystem.cz/robots.txt — all terminated with 'too many redirects (exceeded 10)'.

result.result_summary: GEM System recorded as unverified with a redirect-loop blocker. The host resolves and responds at every variant, so the site is very likely live; the loop pattern is characteristic of www/non-www or locale negotiation failing against a cookieless client.

why_it_matters: One of ten seed actors is entirely uncharacterised, so its banking references (if any) are unknown. The failure mode is a client limitation rather than a source problem, which means it is cheaply fixable with a cookie-enabled headless fetch — it should not be written off.

description: Unicorn's sitemap (https://unicorn.com/sitemap.xml, ~168 URLs across root, /en/ and /cs/ prefixes) contains news pages (news-archiv-unicorn-all, news-detail, news-coworkers), company pages (unicorn-group-profile, mission, history), service pages and product pages (Unicorn Universe), but NO dedicated case-study/reference section and NO investor-relations section. Plain fetches of unicorn.com, unicorn.com/cz and the EN news archive returned only the page title because the site is client-side rendered; unicorn.com/cz returned 404 (the Czech prefix is /cs/).

result.result_summary: Unicorn publishes no public reference or case-study library and no IR section on this domain, and what it does publish is not retrievable without JavaScript execution. unicornsystems.eu 301-redirects to unicorn.com, so it is an alias rather than a second source.

why_it_matters: Unicorn is a large Czech software house with known banking delivery, but it is structurally silent about named clients on the open web — so for this actor the vendor-newsroom channel that underpins the whole cell rationale does not function. Coverage of Unicorn's bank work must come from other channels: Sbirka listin filings, procurement records, and trade press. It also warns that sitemap presence, not homepage fetch, is the only reliable change-detection primitive for JS-rendered vendor sites.

description: Four of the cell's relevant domains have migrated and answer only via redirect: www.trask.cz 301 to www.thetrask.com; www.i.cz 301 to www.iczgroup.com; adastra.cz and www.adastragrp.com to adastracorp.com (and /cs/); www.computerworld.cz 301 to www.computertrends.cz. Separately, the bare host systemonline.cz fails TLS certificate validation ('not in the cert's altnames') and only www.systemonline.cz is usable.

result.result_summary: Legacy domain lists for this cell are stale. All redirects observed were single-hop and well-formed, so the underlying sources are healthy — only the addresses changed.

why_it_matters: Any historical source registry or monitoring config built on the old domains will either fail or silently follow redirects without updating provenance, corrupting the audit trail. The systemonline.cz TLS mismatch in particular produces a hard failure that looks like a dead source but is only a hostname error — always store the www form.

description: An attempt to locate the Czech National Bank's public procurement page at https://www.cnb.cz/cs/o_cnb/verejne-zakazky/ returned HTTP 404. The correct path for the CNB profil zadavatele was not established within this slice, and no CNB procurement URL is asserted.

result.result_summary: No CNB procurement source recorded. This is a negative finding rather than a guessed URL.

why_it_matters: The CNB is both a bank and a contracting authority, so its supplier awards are one of the few fully public records of a Czech bank buying technology — a direct complement to this cell's vendor-side sources. The gap is a missed high-value channel, not a dead end; the correct path needs to be found via the CNB site navigation or the procurement gazette.

description: The session's WebSearch budget (200/200 calls) was already exhausted before this scout issued a single query, so NONE of the assigned seed queries could be run through a search engine. Fallback search endpoints were then attempted and all failed: DuckDuckGo HTML and Lite endpoints served a CAPTCHA challenge ('Select all squares containing a duck'), Mojeek returned HTTP 403, and Bing's RSS output endpoint (bing.com/search?...&format=rss) returned cache-collided results unrelated to the query — a query for '"Diebold Nixdorf" "Czech Republic" bank ATM press release' returned ten Italian-language Lionel Messi quiz pages, and vendor-name queries returned only navigational homepage results with the long-tail terms silently dropped.

result.result_summary: All discovery in this slice was therefore done by first-principles reasoning about source categories, direct URL navigation to vendor domains, redirect-chain following, and ON-SITE search endpoints (which did work — Temenos site search returned the Czech evidence). Recall is consequently structurally biased toward vendors whose domains could be guessed and away from long-tail or unexpected actors.

why_it_matters: This slice should be treated as high-precision but incomplete recall. A re-run of this cell with a working search budget is likely to add materially new candidates, particularly smaller vendors and Czech-language items that only a search index would surface.

description: Czech-language keyword search through a search engine — the mandatory cs-language leg of the method — could not be executed for the same budget reason. The Czech seed query 'Diebold Nixdorf NCR Atleos tisková zpráva Česká republika banka bankomaty' was never run. Czech-language coverage in this slice was instead achieved by navigating directly to Czech-language sources and reading them in Czech (protext.cz, bankovnictvionline.cz, systemonline.cz, lupa.cz) and by building the cs glossary from first principles.

result.result_summary: Three Czech-language sources were verified live and are included as candidates (ČTK Protext finance and IT categories, Bankovnictví online, IT Systems/SystemOnLine). Czech terms actually used against live sites: tisková zpráva, tiskové zprávy, bankomat, finance a ekonomika, IT komunikace a elektronika, vyhledávání, zprávy, banky a finance, banky a finanční organizace, přehledy, technologie, regulace, komerční přílohy, Komerční banka, Česká republika. Terms built but NOT yet exercised against any index: platební terminál, jádrový bankovní systém, samoobslužná zóna, recyklace hotovosti, výroční zpráva, případová studie, nasazení, implementace, dodavatel.

why_it_matters: Czech-language discovery is present but shallow. Any Czech-language vendor announcement that lives outside these three portals is currently invisible to this cell.

description: No Czech-language edition of any global banking-technology vendor site in this cell was located. https://www.dieboldnixdorf.com/cs-cz returned HTTP 500. Comarch's finance news section explicitly offers EN/PL/DE/FR/IT/ES/PT and no Czech option, and www.comarch.cz resolved to a parked domain (certificate issued for parking.domeny.tv). Printec's Czech entry point could not be established: printecgroup.com paths returned 403 and https://www.printec.cz/ failed TLS validation with a self-signed certificate.

result.result_summary: Working hypothesis for this cell: the global vendors publish Czech-relevant material in English only, and any Czech-language version reaches the market through the ČTK Protext wire or Czech trade press rather than through a vendor-owned .cz property. This is exactly the language asymmetry the cell rationale predicted.

why_it_matters: Confirms the collection design: monitor global vendor newsrooms in EN, and monitor Czech-language pickup separately via Protext and the trade press. Do not expect a vendor-owned Czech newsroom to exist.

description: Two vendor case-study libraries were read in full and neither contains a Czech customer. Diebold Nixdorf's banking case studies currently list Bankart, IPAK YULI Bank (Uzbekistan), GHS Federal Credit Union, Cooperative Bank of Kielce (Poland), America First Credit Union, Banca Raiffeisen Locarno (Switzerland) and JN Bank. NCR Atleos's Customer Stories are almost entirely US credit unions with Santander UK as the only European entry.

result.result_summary: By contrast Temenos does carry a Czech reference (Komerční banka, both a selection release and a go-live release plus a success story). So the Czech reference asymmetry across vendors is real and measurable.

why_it_matters: This is a genuine competitor-positioning finding, not just an absence: on their own public evidence, Temenos has a marquee Czech core-banking reference while Diebold Nixdorf and NCR Atleos publicise none. It also means the case-study libraries are worth monitoring as tripwires rather than as current sources of Czech content.

description: A consistent WAF/bot-defence pattern blocked six otherwise-central sources from this fetcher: Finastra press-media (403 on three path variants), Printec Group (403 on three paths), Asseco Central Europe at ce.asseco.com (403), Finextra retail-banking channel (403), SEC EDGAR full-text and browse-edgar endpoints (403, User-Agent policy), and Fiserv newsroom (two 60s timeouts). Thales Group's corporate press-release page returned an empty document body on two path variants, consistent with client-side rendering or a consent gate.

result.result_summary: NONE of these is recorded as dead. 403-with-no-body and repeated timeouts are the signature of edge bot rules, and in SEC's case the 403 is documented policy for clients that do not declare a contact User-Agent. Euronet is a separate case: a 301 from euronetworldwide.com/news to euronet.com/news that itself 404s indicates a site migration, i.e. moved.

why_it_matters: The collection layer for this cell must be provisioned with a headless browser and realistic headers, plus a compliant declaring User-Agent for SEC. Without that, roughly a third of the cell's highest-value sources will look permanently unavailable when they are merely defended.

description: Lupa.cz was fetched and assessed as a candidate Czech-language channel and deliberately NOT included. It is a Czech internet/technology portal whose visible content on the day of assessment covered AI, healthcare digitisation, cloud infrastructure, 3D printing and quantum computing, with no banking IT, fintech or payments coverage in evidence, and no RSS link visible.

result.result_summary: Rejected for this cell on relevance grounds rather than reachability. Bankovnictví online and SystemOnLine cover the same country with far higher banking-technology density.

why_it_matters: Documents a deliberate exclusion so a later run does not re-litigate it, and keeps the candidate list precision-weighted rather than padded.

description: NCR Atleos's own investor newsroom carries the release 'Shareholders Overwhelmingly Vote to Approve Brink's Acquisition of NCR Atleos' dated 30 June 2026, alongside Q2 2026 results dated 5 August 2026.

result.result_summary: The investor.ncratleos.com domain, its RSS feed and its numeric /detail/<id>/ archive are all at material risk of retirement or redirection into Brink's investor infrastructure once the transaction closes.

why_it_matters: This is the single best-automatable endpoint in the cell (real RSS, stable IDs). If it is not mirrored before close, the historical ATM-vendor announcement archive for CEE could become materially harder to reconstruct, and a live monitor would silently go quiet rather than error.

description: The WebSearch tool returned 'this session has used its web search budget (200 of 200 WebSearch calls)' on the very first query attempt, so no search-engine query — Czech or English — could be executed during this cell.

result.result_summary: All discovery was performed instead by direct HTTP fetch of candidate association domains, robots.txt/sitemap.xml enumeration, and recursive link-graph snowballing. This worked well for the six named associations (all six located and mapped) but eliminated the long-tail discovery path that would surface smaller or newer associations whose domains cannot be guessed.

why_it_matters: Coverage of the six seeded associations is thorough and evidence-backed, but the cell cannot claim completeness for Czech financial-sector associations generally. Any association without a guessable domain and without an inbound link from the ones crawled is invisible to this pass.

description: The Czech Fintech Association's official press release category at https://czechfintech.cz/category/tiskove-zpravy/ appears abandoned.

result.result_summary: The newest items retrieved are dated Kvě (May) 2022 and Bře (March) 2022 — the latter announcing Miroslav Lukeš and Ondřej Machač taking over the association's leadership. Meanwhile the same site's /clanky/ stream carries items dated 14-20 August 2026, so the site is live; only this category is dormant.

why_it_matters: Anyone monitoring ČEFTAS via the obvious 'tiskové zprávy' URL would wrongly conclude the association is inactive, and would miss four years of activity. Monitoring must target /clanky/ and /udalosti/ instead, or the WordPress /feed/.

description: Member rosters at three of the six target associations are not present in server-rendered HTML.

result.result_summary: ČLFA /o-nas/clenske-spolecnosti returned 9,253 bytes of navigation and breadcrumb with zero company names; czechfintech.cz /clenove/ returned 274,188 bytes containing the headings 'Řádní členové' and 'Přidružení členové' but no member names (logo-image rendering); AKAT /Clenove-asociace returned 37,722 bytes with the same headings and no names. By contrast ČBA /o-nas/clenove and APEK /seznam-clenu rendered their full rosters in plain HTML.

why_it_matters: Three of the cell's most valuable enumerations require headless-browser collection rather than simple HTTP, which changes the cost and fragility profile of the collection pipeline. The ČEFTAS case may have a cheaper workaround via its exposed WordPress REST API at /wp-json/wp/v2/.

description: ČBA's robots.txt disallows the storage path that appears to hold its annual report PDFs.

result.result_summary: https://www.cbaonline.cz/robots.txt contains 'Disallow: /api/', 'Disallow: /cba_online/' and 'Disallow: /journal_files_storage/'. The /o-nas/vyrocni-zpravy index renders 16 dated rows (2011 through 2026-05-26) with 'Zobrazit PDF' controls, but a static fetch of that page yielded no .pdf hrefs at all — the links are injected client-side and resolve into the disallowed storage area.

why_it_matters: Automated harvesting of ČBA annual reports would breach the site's stated crawler policy. The compliant routes are manual retrieval, or a direct request to the ČBA press office. This is a policy constraint, not a technical one, and should be flagged to whoever configures the collector.

description: ČBA's main site is largely client-rendered, hiding most of its content from plain HTTP clients.

result.result_summary: https://www.cbaonline.cz/ returned 55,021 bytes but only 7 navigable links, and topic pages such as /stranky/pro-media, /stranky/pruzkumy-a-indexy and /stranky/prognozy returned nothing but the page title and nav chrome. Two independent WebFetch attempts on the homepage and /o-nas both reported that member, annual-report and press-release links were absent. The content was only recoverable via robots.txt -> sitemap.xml, which exposed 2,838 URLs including all 28 structural /stranky/ and /o-nas/ pages.

why_it_matters: A naive crawler would grade ČBA — the single most important association in this cell — as a near-empty site. The sitemap-first approach should be the documented default for this domain, and is a transferable technique for other JS-heavy Czech association sites.

description: Česká asociace pojišťoven (cap.cz) could not be fetched.

result.result_summary: curl returned error 56 'Recv failure: Connection reset by peer' with HTTP code 000 — the connection was reset mid-response rather than refused or 404'd.

why_it_matters: This pattern is characteristic of bot defence (TLS-fingerprint or user-agent filtering) on a live site, not of a dead host. Per the run's hard rules this is recorded as a hypothesis requiring the deterministic verification pass; it must not be marked dead. ČAP matters because bancassurance is a material fee-income line for Czech banks.

description: AKAT's 'Monitoring trhu' section is dormant despite the rest of the site being current.

result.result_summary: The newest item on https://www.akatcr.cz/Asociace-AKAT/Monitoring-trhu is a February 2019 TV interview with Jana Brodani about mutual fund investing. AKAT's press release and annual report sections are by contrast current to August 2026.

why_it_matters: The section name promises exactly what a market-intelligence collector wants and delivers seven-year-old content. The live equivalents are /Zverejnena-data and /Dokumenty/Tiskova-zprava-AKAT; the collector configuration should skip Monitoring trhu.

description: APEK states two different member counts on two of its own properties.

result.result_summary: https://www.apek.cz/seznam-clenu states 'Celkem je vylistováno 570 členů' across 64 pages, while https://data.apek.cz/ describes APEK as a 'sdružení více než 650 podnikatelů' (association of more than 650 entrepreneurs).

why_it_matters: The figures differ by roughly 14 percent. Either the data site is stale, or the directory excludes some membership class. Any headline citing APEK membership size must state which source and date it came from; the directory count is the defensible one because it is enumerable.

description: No Czech crypto-asset or digital-asset industry association was located in this cell.

result.result_summary: With WebSearch unavailable, no crypto-industry association domain could be discovered, and none of the six seeded associations linked to one. The nearest observed signal was editorial coverage of a euro stablecoin on the ČEFTAS /clanky/ stream — topical interest without an identified representative body.

why_it_matters: MiCA implementation makes crypto-asset service providers a live competitive and regulatory topic for Czech banks and payment firms. If a Czech CASP association exists, it is an unmapped pointer source. No URL is asserted here because none was found — guessing one would be fabrication.

description: No dedicated Czech association of non-bank payment institutions or payment service providers was identified.

result.result_summary: Non-bank acquirers and PSPs do appear in Czech industry data — SBK's statistics contributor list names ComGate Payments, EVO Payments, Global Payments, Nexi, Euronet, KB Smart Pay, Twisto Payments and Direct Fidoo Payments — but they surface as data contributors to SBK, not as members of any PSP-specific trade body found in this pass.

why_it_matters: It is plausible that no such Czech association exists and that SBK plus ČEFTAS jointly occupy that representational space. That is itself a useful structural finding: for Czech non-bank payments actors, SBK's contributor roster is the best available enumeration and should be treated as the primary registry for that segment.

description: Two collection-relevant encoding and URL hazards were observed that will silently corrupt a naive collector.

result.result_summary: First, the SBK and CardMag sites are legacy hand-built pages served in a Czech single-byte encoding — extracted text loses all diacritics under a UTF-8 assumption ('Sdružení' rendered as 'Sdruen', 'platebních karet' as 'platebnch karet'). Second, AKAT's DNN platform encodes Czech characters as decimal HTML entities inside URL slugs, e.g. '/Dokumenty/Vyrocni-zpravy/v253rocn237-zpr225va-20232024' for 'výroční zpráva'. Third, several SBK homepage hrefs are malformed, missing the slash after the host (e.g. 'http://aktuality.bankovnikarty.czTZ_MasterCard_18-08-2026.pdf').

why_it_matters: Each hazard produces silent failures rather than errors: mangled Czech entity names that will not match any actor map, unmatched URL patterns, and 'dead link' false positives on SBK that are actually authoring typos. All three need explicit handling in the collector.

description: The WebSearch tool was unavailable for this entire slice: the first search call returned 'this session has used its web search budget (200 of 200 WebSearch calls)'. Both attempted Czech-language queries ('ČTK Protext tisková zpráva distribuce banka platební služby' and 'Protext ČTK distribuce tiskových zpráv ceník archiv') were refused before execution.

result.result_summary: No SERP-based discovery was possible. All 30+ sources below were found instead by direct fetch of known/inferred Czech domains and by link-snowballing homepages, footers and category pages. Czech-language coverage was still achieved (all navigation, terms and paths used were Czech), but a cs-language search sweep of the seed queries has not been performed and this slice should not be treated as a completed cs-search pass.

why_it_matters: Long-tail actors that have no guessable domain — small payment institutions, credit unions (spořitelní a úvěrní družstva), niche fintechs, PR agencies with financial clients — are exactly the ones a search sweep would surface and a domain-guessing sweep will miss. The cell's stated rationale (catching entities too small to have discoverable IR sections) is therefore only partly served.

description: financninoviny.cz, historically ČTK's dedicated economic/financial news domain, no longer serves its own site.

result.result_summary: https://www.financninoviny.cz/ returns HTTP 301 Moved Permanently to http://www.ceskenoviny.cz/ekonomika/.

why_it_matters: Any stored source registry entry or historical citation pointing at financninoviny.cz should be remapped to ceskenoviny.cz/ekonomika/. The economic wire has been folded into the general ČTK consumer site rather than discontinued.

description: No public entry point to ČTK's Infobanka news archive could be located.

result.result_summary: https://www.ctk.cz/sluzby/infobanka/ returned HTTP 404, and ibsearch.ctk.cz did not resolve at all (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND). Infobanka is named as a service on https://www.ctk.cz/sluzby/ but the product page path is different from the obvious guess.

why_it_matters: Infobanka is the deep historical archive of Czech agency reporting and the natural back-catalogue for banking and payments announcements older than the free web archive. Access will require going through ČTK commercially (ctk@ctk.cz, +420 222 098 111) rather than finding a public URL.

description: csob.cz refuses automated fetches across every path attempted.

result.result_summary: HTTP 500 Internal Server Error on /portal/csob/pro-media, /portal/o-csob/pro-media and /pro-media. A 500 rather than a 404 indicates the host answered and withheld content — consistent with edge bot defence, not with a missing page.

why_it_matters: ČSOB is one of the largest Czech banking and payments groups; leaving it uncollected would be a material gap. Recorded as blocked-but-live, not dead. Interim workarounds: the ČTK Protext wire and the KBC Group newsroom.

description: Several financial-sector hosts returned WAF-style 403s to this fetcher.

result.result_summary: HTTP 403 Forbidden on https://www.unicreditbank.cz/, https://www.creditas.cz/ and https://www.mastercard.com/news/europe/cs-cz/. All three are near-certainly live sites behind bot filtering.

why_it_matters: These are hypotheses about accessibility, not verdicts about liveness. They should be routed to a browser-based collector rather than marked dead, and their newsroom paths remain unconfirmed — no path was invented for them here.

description: Two Czech media-monitoring vendors could not be reached because of TLS errors from this environment.

result.result_summary: https://www.anopress.cz/ failed with 'certificate has expired'; https://www.monitora.cz/ failed with 'self signed certificate'. Both errors occurred before any HTTP response, so nothing is known about the sites' content or liveness.

why_it_matters: These are the main alternatives to NEWTON Media for retrospective archives of Czech coverage. The identical class of failure across two unrelated hosts suggests a local TLS-interception artefact rather than two simultaneous vendor outages, so they must be re-verified rather than dropped.

description: globalpaymentseurope.eu no longer presents a valid certificate for its own name.

result.result_summary: Fetch failed with 'Hostname/IP does not match certificate's altnames: Host: www.globalpaymentseurope.eu is not in the cert's altnames: DNS:0oo1.cz, DNS:www.0oo1.cz' — the hostname now resolves to infrastructure serving an unrelated domain.

why_it_matters: Global Payments Europe was a significant Czech card-processing actor. The certificate mismatch is evidence that the web presence has been retired, rebranded or absorbed, which means its announcement channel needs to be re-identified under whatever the current corporate name is. Recorded as an unresolved lead, not as a dead company.

description: Three financial companies exposed no media section from their homepage navigation.

result.result_summary: visa.cz homepage showed no 'tiskové zprávy', 'pro média' or newsroom links at all. jtbank.cz (J&T Banka) exposed only contacts, wealth report and investment-services links. partnersbanka.cz exposed only /o-nas, /pobocky and /kontakty. In each case the homepage was fetched successfully — the links are genuinely absent from it, though a section may exist deeper in the site.

why_it_matters: This is precisely the pattern the cell exists to handle: where no corporate newsroom is discoverable, the ČTK Protext wire and the media-monitoring archives become the only systematic capture route for that actor. For Visa specifically, Czech announcements appear to run through the global newsroom or through partner releases — a Visa Czech Top Shop item was observed on the Protext finance feed, issued by a third party (INSTORE CONSULTING EU), not by Visa.

description: The 'obvious' Czech newsroom path /o-nas/pro-media or /o-bance/pro-media is unreliable across the sector.

result.result_summary: 404s were returned by moneta.cz/o-nas/pro-media (real path: /servis-pro-media/tiskove-zpravy), rb.cz/o-nas/pro-media (real path: /informacni-servis/pro-media), airbank.cz/o-air-bank/pro-media/ (real path: /pro-novinare/) and cbaonline.cz/tiskove-zpravy (association 404 page). fio.cz/o-nas/pro-media resolved to the homepage rather than a newsroom (real path: /spolecnost-fio/media/tiskove-zpravy). Only kb.cz and csas.cz matched the guessed pattern.

why_it_matters: Any collector built on a path template will silently lose most of the sector, and stored registry URLs will rot. Newsroom URLs must be resolved per-entity from homepage navigation and re-resolved periodically. The local vocabulary is broader than 'pro média': 'pro novináře', 'servis pro média', 'informační servis', 'tiskové centrum' and plain 'média' all occur.

description: Machine-readable feeds are largely missing from Czech bank newsrooms.

result.result_summary: No RSS feed was visible on the media sections of Komerční banka, MONETA, mBank CZ or Air Bank. RSS was confirmed only for Česká národní banka (footer link /cs/obecne/rss/) and for ceskenoviny.cz (footer RSS link). MONETA and the Prague Stock Exchange offer email newsletters instead.

why_it_matters: Collection for this cell will be poll-and-diff HTML crawling rather than feed subscription for most corporate newsrooms, which raises both latency and fragility. It also strengthens the case for treating the ČTK wire as the primary rail: one crawlable, paginated, searchable archive covering many actors at once.

description: Several newsroom listing pages returned navigation-only shells to a plain HTTP fetch.

result.result_summary: kb.cz/cs/o-bance/tiskove-zpravy, csas.cz/cs/o-nas/pro-media/tiskove-zpravy, rb.cz/informacni-servis/pro-media/tiskove-zpravy and cbaonline.cz/stranky/pro-media all returned headers and menus with no release items, despite HTTP 200. Items were visible on the parent /pro-media pages for KB and ČS.

why_it_matters: These are client-rendered listings, not empty archives. A headless browser is required for collection; a naive crawler would record these high-value banks as having zero press releases.

description: No Czech-language competitor to ČTK Protext was identified in this run.

result.result_summary: Protext (ČTK) and NEWTON Media's PR Studio are the only Czech press-release distribution products confirmed by fetch. No second national wire was found, and without WebSearch it was not possible to test for smaller or defunct distributors, so no local-language terms for such competitors could be gathered.

why_it_matters: If Protext is effectively the single national wire, the collection design has a single point of failure and a single point of leverage. That conclusion is plausible from what was observed but is not established — it rests on absence of evidence produced by a tool constraint, not on a completed search.

description: The session's WebSearch budget (200/200 calls) was already exhausted by earlier agents before this scout issued its first query. Both attempted seed queries — 'Hospodářské noviny banka hospodářské výsledky zisk čtvrtletí' (cs) and 'Seznam Zprávy Aktuálně banky výsledky platby analýza' (cs) — were refused by the tool with a budget message, and no further cs or en search-engine queries could be run.

result.result_summary: Zero search-engine results obtained. Discovery was carried out entirely by direct fetching of candidate domains and by snowballing section trees, publisher names and RSS paths out of the fetched navigation of each site.

why_it_matters: Search-engine discovery is how you find the outlets you did not already think of — smaller CZ business titles, journalist blogs, newsletter products, tag pages for individual banks. This slice is therefore strong on the named backbone outlets and structurally verified section URLs, but weaker on long-tail discovery than a normal run. A re-run with search budget should be scheduled before this cell is considered complete.

description: Both MAFRA-group domains named in the cell brief — ekonomika.idnes.cz and www.lidovky.cz — were refused by the fetch tool itself with 'Claude Code is unable to fetch from <host>'. This is a client-side domain block, not a server response.

result.result_summary: No structural verification of iDNES Ekonomika or Lidovky Ekonomika: section paths, RSS feeds and paywall model remain unconfirmed. Both are recorded as candidates with blocked=true and reduced confidence, NOT as dead.

why_it_matters: iDNES is one of the highest-reach Czech news portals and Lidovky is a quality daily; missing their feed structure leaves a hole in mass-reach amplification signal. A browser-based pass (Chrome MCP) or a plain HTTP client outside this tool should recover them cheaply.

description: Four further hosts failed on transport or bot-defence grounds: monitora.cz and www.monitora.cz ('self signed certificate'), www.anopress.cz ('certificate has expired'), www.denik.cz/ekonomika/ (HTTP 403), english.radio.cz (HTTP 403).

result.result_summary: None of these could be structurally verified. Per the playbook, 403s and TLS failures are treated as bot-defended-or-environment issues, i.e. hypotheses, not liveness verdicts.

why_it_matters: Two of them (Monitora, Anopress) are aggregator/archive routes that would materially reduce the cost and legal risk of collecting paywalled CZ coverage, so they are worth re-testing rather than dropping.

description: Several guessed section URLs did not resolve: seznamzpravy.cz/sekce/ekonomika-11 returned the World desk rather than economics (correct IDs are ekonomika-194 and ekonomika-finance-299, recovered from the homepage nav); denikn.cz/rubrika/byznys/ 404'd (correct path /ekonomika/ plus tag pages); info.cz/ekonomika 404'd; echo24.cz/ekonomika 404'd; newtonmedia.eu/cs 404'd; forbes.cz/rubrika/byznys/ 301-redirected to a 2014 CDN image file.

result.result_summary: Section IDs and paths in the Czech mainstream media are not guessable and several are stale; all confirmed paths in this slice were taken from fetched navigation, not assumed.

why_it_matters: Any crawler for this cell must resolve section URLs from live navigation at build time and re-validate them periodically, otherwise feeds will silently go empty after a site relaunch. The Forbes case shows a redirect can point at a legacy asset and still return 301, which naive crawlers will treat as success.

description: Apart from E15's explicit 'Finance a bankovnictví' section, no outlet in this cell was confirmed to expose a standing banking-only landing page. HN uses byznys.hn.cz, Seznam Zprávy uses a general Finance sub-desk, Aktuálně and ČT24 use a general Ekonomika rubric.

why_it_matters: A collection plan that relies only on open sources will systematically capture wire copy and consumer-facing amplification while missing the executive comment and unpublished figures that are the stated reason this cell exists. Budget for 3-4 subscription seats or a Newton/Monitora licence.

description: No parent group in this cell publishes a Czech-language investor-relations channel. description: UniCredit's 'Financial Reports from our Countries' index returned HTTP 403 Forbidden on direct fetch. The same host serves /content/dam/ PDF assets that were referenced successfully from search results.

result.result_summary: 403 with no response body, 2026-08-25. Treated as a bot/WAF defence hypothesis, not as a dead or removed page.

why_it_matters: The deterministic verification pass should retry this with browser-class headers before any liveness verdict; recording it as dead would wrongly remove the group-maintained pointer to UniCredit Bank Czech Republic and Slovakia's statutory reporting.

description: For the ATM/self-service hardware and services parents (Diebold Nixdorf, NCR Atleos, Nexi), no Czech-specific disclosure was found in group financial reporting.

result.result_summary: Only marketing artefacts surfaced — e.g. a Diebold Nixdorf customer case study on end-to-end ATM network outsourcing for ČSOB (99.8% uptime, 99.98% cash availability). Nexi produced no Czech-specific hit at all.

why_it_matters: For these vendors the useful group-level channel is case studies and press releases, not segment reporting. They belong in a vendor/supplier cell rather than in parent-group investor reporting, and should not be tracked here at earnings cadence.

why_it_matters: One of the two anchor portals in this cell is undocumented. Its comparison tables, fee coverage and company-data sections are unmapped, so any completeness claim for the Czech consumer-finance comparison layer is currently false. Per the run's hard rules this is a hypothesis of bot defence, NOT a liveness verdict.

It should be re-probed (http:// as well as https://, and a site-scoped search of mesec.cz) before being written off - a single refused connection is not proof the award is dead.

description: Investujeme.cz's dedicated banking section at https://www.investujeme.cz/bankovnictvi/ rendered a single article dated 2022-09-20, about banking and insurance recruitment and salary levels, with no product, fee, ATM-network or executive coverage.

result.result_summary: The banking taxonomy node is either abandoned or the live banking coverage has moved to a path not discoverable without search. Homepage-level banking and mortgage coverage does appear current.

why_it_matters: A collector pointed at /bankovnictvi/ would silently return nothing for years and look like a healthy but quiet feed. The active path must be re-mapped before this source is wired up.

description: Kurzy.cz banking verticals (/banky/, /banky/sazebniky/, /bankomaty/) returned only the site header, publisher identification (Kurzy.cz, spol. s r.o. and AliaWeb, spol. s r.o.), navigation, and a user-authentication message. No section body was returned on any of the three fetches. No 404 and no 403 was raised.

result.result_summary: Three fetches, three empty bodies with HTTP success. Hypothesis: client-side rendering, or a registration gate, or aggressive markup stripping in conversion - not a dead section.

why_it_matters: A potential fourth independent normalisation of Czech bank sazebnik and ATM data is unassessed. If it renders under a headless browser it is a valuable cross-check; if it is login-gated it should be dropped in favour of the banks' own sazebnik PDFs. It must not be recorded as dead.

description: Two outlets whose names implied strong fit turned out to under-deliver on this cell's topics on inspection. FinTag.cz, despite the fintech-suggestive name, published general economics and politics (US debt, Ukraine, pharma) rather than Czech retail-bank product or fee detail. result.result_summary: Both are recorded as low-priority candidates with the shortfall documented rather than dropped, so a future run does not re-discover them and re-inflate expectations from the name alone.

why_it_matters: Prevents wasted collector capacity and stops name-based optimism from inflating the apparent density of the Czech specialist-media layer.

description: Local-language (cs) coverage was achieved despite the search outage: every candidate but none-excepted was fetched at a Czech-language property, and Czech domain terms were used constructively to locate sources - 'bankovni poplatky' produced bankovnipoplatky.com/.cz, 'sazebniky' and 'bankomaty' produced the Kurzy.cz vertical paths, 'banky' produced banky.cz, and 'poradci sobe' produced the adviser community. description: WebSearch was unavailable for the entire run: the first two search calls (the Czech-language seeds 'CzechCrunch fintech investice platby startup kolo financování' and 'Lupa.cz platební technologie banka fintech') both returned 'this session has used its web search budget (200 of 200 WebSearch calls)'. Czech-language coverage was still achieved — Czech terms were used against on-site search and Czech tag paths (/n/fintech/, /n/platby/, /n/bankovnictvi/, /tag/fintech/) — but no engine-mediated Czech-language discovery took place.

why_it_matters: Direct fetching only finds sources you can already guess the domain of. Small Czech fintech blogs, personal Substack-style newsletters, LinkedIn-native commentators and independent podcasts are exactly the long-tail this cell was scoped to catch, and they are effectively invisible without a search engine. description: CzechCrunch does not appear to expose a dedicated fintech tag or topic archive. https://cc.cz/tema/fintech/ returned homepage-style content rather than a tag archive (a soft 404), and the confirmed rubric list from the homepage (/byznys/, /startupy/, /tech/, /investice/, /e-commerce/, /krypto/, /umela-inteligence/ and others) contains no fintech rubric.

description: https://cc.cz/eventy/fintech-week-cee-2026/ appeared in CzechCrunch on-site search results for 'fintech', but fetching it returned the general CzechCrunch events index (People, Money Maker Praha, Longevity Festival 2027, Future 2027, CzechCrunch X, plus supported events) with no Fintech Week CEE content at all.

description: https://ceftas.visualbook.pro/, linked from the Czech Fintech Association's projects page, was hypothesised to be a fintech company map or directory. It is not — it is the association's brand and visual identity guidebook (logos, typography, colours, naming conventions, contact ondra@czechfintech.cz), available in Czech, Slovak and English.

result.result_summary: No fintech company map, catalogue or landscape graphic was found on the association's site. The usable actor lists are the member directory at /clenove/ (80+ members) and the CzechTrade export brochure at /project/10647/ (200+ active firms).

why_it_matters: Prevents a downstream collector from wasting effort parsing a brand style guide as a company database, and redirects effort to the two lists that actually contain company names.

description: A 'FinTech Roadmap' podcast was hypothesised as a Czech Fintech Association partnership and specifically searched for on both https://czechfintech.cz/clanky/ and https://czechfintech.cz/projekty/. Neither page mentions it. The association's confirmed projects are the Studie českého fintechu, the Enterprise Investment Scheme (EIS) initiative, and the CzechTrade export brochure.

The podcasts actually confirmed are general-business (CzechCrunch Money Maker, 201 eps), general-tech (Lupa.cz podcast), and adjacent HN shows (MoneyPenny on personal finance, Krypto Insider on crypto). description: The StartupJobs.cz magazine path https://www.startupjobs.cz/magazin returned HTTP 404. The blog at https://www.startupjobs.cz/blog does exist and is live, but its content is HR-focused — hiring, interviews, compensation, workplace culture, monthly labour-market notes (e.g. /blog/clanek/co-cervenec-posunul-vpred-7-26).

result.result_summary: No coverage of Czech startup funding rounds, capital raises or company launches was found on the StartupJobs blog. It does not belong in a funding/launch monitoring pipeline.

why_it_matters: StartupJobs is a plausible-looking startup-ecosystem property that would waste a collection slot. Its residual value is as a hiring-signal source (a payments startup posting many roles is a growth signal), which is a different workstream from A1.

description: SMARTmania.cz (Czech consumer tech portal, founded 2005, redakce@smartmania.cz) was probed as a possible mobile-payments channel (Apple Pay, Google Pay, banking apps). The retrieved homepage showed only smartphones, smartwatches, keyboards, drones and automotive content, with categories under /kategorie/recenze/ and a product catalogue at /katalog/.

result.result_summary: No evidence of payments, banking-app or Czech bank launch coverage was found. Registration-gated perks exist but no paywall or RSS was visible.

why_it_matters: Rules out one of the obvious consumer-tech candidates for wallet/contactless coverage and narrows where that signal actually lives — Lupa.cz /n/platby/ carried the contactless-wearables story (Huawei watches, 13.4.2026) instead.

description: Five plausible Czech sources returned HTTP 403 Forbidden with no response body on a single plain fetch each: https://www.penize.cz/, https://www.investicniweb.cz/, https://www.zive.cz/, https://www.ecommercebridge.cz/ and https://finmag.cz/. A 403 with no body is the signature of bot protection, not of a dead site.

result.result_summary: All five are recorded as blocked=true and unverified rather than dead. Four are carried as candidates with reduced confidence (0.30-0.35); Finmag.cz is recorded here only, as nothing at all about its current structure could be confirmed.

why_it_matters: If these are logged as dead, the run permanently loses the merchant-acceptance angle (Ecommerce Bridge) and two significant consumer-finance archives. They must be re-probed with a headless browser or realistic headers before any liveness verdict is issued.

description: Two domains failed below the HTTP layer rather than returning a status code: https://tyinternety.cz/ failed with 'connect ECONNREFUSED 167.99.132.26:443' (DNS resolved, TLS connection refused), and https://depo.ventures/ failed with 'getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND depo.ventures' (no DNS record at all).

result.result_summary: TyInternety.cz — a Czech digital/marketing trade title — could not be assessed. Depo Ventures, hypothesised as a publisher of a Czech startup funding report, has no resolving domain under that name; the Czech startup funding report hypothesis is unconfirmed.

why_it_matters: ENOTFOUND is materially stronger evidence than a 403 — the depo.ventures guess was almost certainly just a wrong domain, so the Czech VC-published funding-report layer remains entirely unexplored. TyInternety needs one retry before any conclusion; a single ECONNREFUSED can be transient or geo/IP-specific.

description: Forbes Česko (forbes.cz) — an outlet named explicitly in this coverage cell — returned essentially empty bodies on three separate paths: the homepage, /technologie/ and /tag/fintech/. Each returned only a title/header line ('Forbes | I jedna věta vám může změnit život!', and for the tag page 'Fintech ▶ ... s Forbes Česko | Forbes'), with no navigation, no article list and no URLs.

result.result_summary: Confirmed: HTTP 200 responses and a /tag/<slug>/ URL pattern with a fintech tag that resolves. Unconfirmed: rubric structure, article inventory, paywall model, newsletters, podcasts, RSS.

why_it_matters: Forbes CZ is a named target of this cell and cannot be collected with a plain HTTP client. Any pipeline must budget for headless rendering, or find a sitemap/RSS bypass, before Forbes coverage can be claimed.

Terms actually exercised: fintech, fintechové startupy, platby, platební brána, platební metody, bezkontaktní platby, bankovnictví, banky, účty a platby, kreditní/charge karty, startupy, investice, kolo financování, evidence tržeb/EET, sandbox, tiskové zprávy, členové, rozhovor, podcast.

description: WebSearch was unavailable for the entire slice: the very first search call returned 'this session has used its web search budget (200 of 200 WebSearch calls)'. No cs-language or en-language query-based discovery could be executed at all.

Any Czech sell-side house, rating-aggregator portal or broker-note archive not linked from patria.cz / kurzy.cz / akcie.cz / roklen24.cz / wood.com / esma.europa.eu is systematically invisible in this slice.

description: Czech-language coverage was achieved through Czech-language page content and Czech navigation terms (doporučení, cílová cena, oficiální sdělení, výsledková sezóna, hospodaření), but NOT through Czech-language search queries, because WebSearch was unusable.

result.result_summary: Czech terminology was harvested and applied against fetched pages, confirming real cs-language research artefacts (e.g. Patria ratings in Czech: Držet / Redukovat; Akcie.cz 'cílová cena 1043 Kč'). However no cs query such as 'analytická zpráva české banky doporučení cílová cena' was ever submitted to a search engine.

description: All three major rating agencies were unreachable by plain fetch. Moody's (ratings.moodys.com) and S&P Global Ratings (spglobal.com/ratings/en/) both returned HTTP 403 Forbidden with no body; Fitch (www.fitchratings.com) was blocked at the fetch layer before any HTTP status was obtained.

result.result_summary: Three of the highest-value sources in this cell are recorded as blocked-but-presumed-live. None is recorded as dead — a 403 on a major commercial site is a bot-defence signature, not evidence of absence.

why_it_matters: Rating actions are the single most informative third-party interrogation of a bank's disclosures. If the collector cannot reach them, the cell loses its highest-credibility layer and falls back on Czech broker portals alone.

description: Attempts to locate ESMA's European Rating Platform (ERP) — the free, official EU database of individual credit ratings issued by registered CRAs — failed on hostname guesses errp.esma.europa.eu and cerep.esma.europa.eu (both ENOTFOUND) and on the path guess /publications-and-data/european-rating-platform (404). The ESMA CRA supervision hub was reached but does not link the ERP or CEREP.

why_it_matters: The ERP would be a free, licence-clean, machine-readable substitute for the three bot-defended commercial agency portals — potentially resolving the highest-severity access problem in this cell. Leaving it unresolved is the biggest unrealised win here.

description: Roklen24, named in the cell brief as a sell-side/analyst-adjacent source, was confirmed live but has narrowed to FX education, currency-pair commentary and an economic calendar. The fetch explicitly found no bank ratings and no traditional analyst research.

result.result_summary: Roklen24 retained at low priority and usefulness 0.3 rather than being carried at the seed's implied weight.

why_it_matters: Prevents the collection pipeline from spending crawl budget and analyst attention on a source that no longer produces the content type this cell needs. The seed list is partially stale and should be corrected upstream.

description: Kurzy.cz per-issuer pages could not be reached. Fetches of https://www.kurzy.cz/akcie-cz/ and https://www.kurzy.cz/akcie-cz/burza/ both returned only global site navigation and the operator notice, with no issuer table and no links for Komerční banka, Moneta or Erste.
